chunks: "Whoever comes to this House for hajj or as a mu'tamir, being free of arrogance, returns from his sins like the state of the day his mother gave birth to him. Arrogance is to be ignorant of the truth and to attack its people, and whoever does that has disputed with Allah over His cloak."

key_terms.الْبَيْتَ: the Sacred House, meaning the Ka'bah, the destination of hajj and 'umrah
key_terms.الْكِبْرِ: arrogance; a pride that rejects truth and opposes its people
key_terms.رِدَاءَهُ: His mantle or cloak, expressing a quality belonging uniquely to Allah

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام describe the role of humility in hajj and 'umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that hajj and 'umrah, when performed free from arrogance, become a means of complete forgiveness of sins. It also defines arrogance as ignorance of the truth and hostility toward its people, showing that spiritual purification depends on humility before Allah and the truth.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2147 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"Whoever visits this House, either for Hajj or Umrah, free from arrogance, returns from their sins as pure as the day their mother gave birth to them. Arrogance is to deny the truth and to attack its people, and whoever does so has contested Allah (swt) for His mantle."
